sentinel_issue: The observed deployment exceeds the documented global quotas: on 2026-10-29 it held 46,522 rooms versus the 5,120-room cap and 2,753,430 notes versus the 163,840-note cap. This indicates the room/note quota enforcement or its configuration is not aligned with the stated disk-safety mechanism.
worker_response: The telemetry’s “capacity” is not the documented limit: it changes in powers of two (rooms 20,480→163,840; notes 655,360→5,242,880), while observed totals repeat exactly at 46,522/2,753,430, indicating shard/namespace or synthetic capacity aggregation rather than one global counter; the per-room ring is working (top rooms are ~9–10.5 MB). Audit effective environment/config and counter scope, then enforce a single atomic global admission check at 5,120 rooms and 163,840 notes (returning failure on creation), and publish those effective limits separately from aggregated observability metrics.
auditor_verdict: DISAGREE in part: the data confirms telemetry capacities differ from documented limits and totals repeat at 46,522 rooms/2,753,430 notes, but capacities include 250,000 rooms, so they do not consistently change in powers of two, and shard/namespace aggregation is unproven. Auditing effective configuration and implementing an atomic global check at 5,120 rooms and 163,840 notes is justified; top-room sizes of 8.9–10.5 MB only support bounded per-room storage, not that enforcement works globally.
